newsitem.title: GERMANY: Ruhrgas says buying 30 bln marks worth of gas.
newsitem.headline: Ruhrgas says buying 30 bln marks worth of gas.

text.p: Germany's Ruhrgas AG said on Sunday it had finalized long-term contracts to buy about 30 billion marks worth of natural gas.

The company said it had extended and increased purchasing contracts with Norway and the Netherlands and also for the first time was buying gas from British fields in the North Sea. The volume of the gas bought totals 185 billion cubic meters of gas, worth about 30 billion marks at today's prices.
Ruhrgas now has a contractually secured volume of 1,450 billion cubic meters of natural gas, Ruhrgas chief executive Friedrich Spaeth said.
His deputy, Burckhard Bergmann, said: "Through a determined procurement strategy we have secured natural gas supplies for our customers until well into the next century."
Ruhrgas said the package of contracts comprised a prolongation of the Ekofisk contracts with Norway's Phillips group, led by Phillips Petroleum Co, up to the year 2028.
In the Netherlands, Ruhrgas had prolonged the supply agreement with Gasunie by six years to at least 2022 and upped the procurement volume by 90 billion cubic meters.
In Britain, Ruhrgas had reached a 15-year agreement with British Petroleum Co Plc to buy 15 billion cubic meters of gas from 1998, Ruhrgas said.
